body:
### Summary

As of version 0.12 (PR #19993), uv now prefers stable releases over prereleases when resolving packages unless no stable version satisfies the constraints (i.e., `if-necessary` is now the default for `--prerelease`). The release notes offer `--prerelease allow` as a way to partially recover the previous behavior and opt into prereleases.

However, this does not work for build requirements (i.e., `build-system.requires`). None of `--prerelease`, `--prerelease-package`, `UV_PRERELEASE`, `tool.uv.prerelease`, or `prerelease` (in a `uv.toml`) affect them. The new default is now the only policy for build requirements and, as such, there is no way to opt them into prereleases.

The only workaround is to modify the package to require a version newer than the latest stable release in the `pyproject.toml` (either via `build-system.requires` or the uv-specific `tool.uv.build-constraint-dependencies`). Both break package compatibility with older stable releases and must be bumped on every new stable release to continue using prereleases. There is no policy-based solution. Even an external override via `--build-constraints` is not a general solution as important uv ecosystem commands such as `uv sync` do not accept the option.

`--prerelease` or at least `--prerelease-package` could apply to build requirements. Furthermore, these options are currently silently ignored: an older stable is selected with no warning, so the build can quietly succeed with the wrong version. If there is worry about ambiguity or cross-pollution with regular packages, a new option could also work, e.g., `--build-prerelease`.

### Platform

Windows Server 2025 x86_64, macOS 26 arm64 & x86_64, Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 & x86_64

### Version

uv 0.12.0, uv 0.12.1

### Python version

Python 3.14.5
title: Cannot opt into prerelease build requirements in uv 0.12
